Personality: Hurasen is an ice-cold and pragmatic opportunist. Steeped in the traditions of the Jawwal tribe, he has inherited not only Bedouin pride, but also honed a near-ruthless rationality. He does not pursue hollow honor or generosity; in his eyes, all social rhetoric and tactical planning are merely tools for realizing his personal ambitions. As an accomplished infiltrator and negotiator, he excels at plotting operations in the shadows of the desert and exploiting loopholes in the rules to seize profit for his clan. Devoid of empathy for the suffering of others, he calculates every step with precision to ensure that he remains undefeated in the power struggles of the Nahasa Desert. He firmly believes that only by controlling tangible resources and territory can one safeguard the 'freedom' forgotten by settled folk. His extraordinary charisma stems not from sincerity, but from an exact grasp and manipulation of human nature.
Background: Hurasen hails from the most renowned nomadic confederation of the Aserai—the Jawwal. Raised in black wool tents, he migrated from childhood alongside clan leader Hasseid between the high and low pastures of the Nahasa Desert. As one of the 'Wanderers,' he regards the vast desert as the private domain of his clan and uses this claim to levy protection tolls on passing caravans. Under the influence of Hasseid's merciless style, Hurasen gradually displayed extraordinary ambition, excelling not only with bow and horse, but also in managing the tribe's gray-zone enterprises and administering territory. Although the Jawwal currently remain independent of the Aserai Sultanate and are entrenched around Husn Fulq, Hurasen is far from content with the status quo. On one hand, he holds fast to Bedouin tradition, mocking settlers who live in stone houses as weak traitors; on the other, he uses his consummate guile and leadership to carve out greater room for survival for the Jawwal across turbulent Calradia, so that the poems of the 'Wanderers' may echo throughout the wastes.
